prompt:
Operator-visibility surfaces: forward-progress, event feed, clocks, and post-mortem retention

## Goal

An operator watching a running pipeline currently cannot distinguish a healthy agent from a wedged one. During a 48-hour run, four distinct pathologies all presented identically in `get_status`: `running`, every agent `WORKING`, no pending decisions. Diagnosing any of them required host-side forensics (git reflog against agent worktrees, orchestrator log greps, racing kubelet GC for pod logs).

Build the surfaces that make those states visible, and the detectors that act on them. **Twelve items in four groups. All twelve are in scope.**

## Before you start: already implemented — do NOT rebuild

These were shipped in #3524 (merged 2026-07-10, an ancestor of current HEAD). A previous attempt at this task wasted a full phase planning to build them again. Verify each yourself, then move on:

- `wait-status` `--exclude-types` / `--quiet`: **both exist**, `skills/sdlc/bin/wait-status:390-402`, helpers `_parse_exclude_types` / `_line_is_essential` / `_should_emit_line`, tests in `orchestrator/tests/test_wait_status_flags.py`.
- `slice.closed` event: **exists**, `EventType.SLICE_CLOSED` at `orchestrator/events.py:56`; emitted from `record_complete` / `record_failure` via injected emitter at `orchestrator/slice_scheduler.py:378-428`; wired at `orchestrator/routes/pipelines/_run_implement.py:86`; present in `_STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES`.
- Rate-limit classification: **done, deliberately differently**. `EX_RATE_LIMITED = 69` at `shared/egg_agent/auth_errors.py:53` -> `shared/egg_agent/__main__.py:162` -> `JOB_OUTCOME_RATE_LIMITED` -> `JobSupervisor.record_rate_limited` at `orchestrator/event_loop/_supervisor.py:293`.
- `overseer_owns_host_detection`: **removed**; grep-clean from source, remaining hits are tests asserting its removal.

WARNING: 429 / "rate limit" / "overloaded" are excluded from `EX_AUTH_FATAL` on purpose. A throttle self-heals; making it credential-fatal is a regression. Do not "fix" this.

## Verification requirement (applies to every item)

Issue text goes stale; the tree is ground truth. For each item, before implementing: check whether it already exists, cite the **file and symbol** you checked, and state a **present or absent** verdict. If present, say so and drop it from scope. An analysis or plan asserting a gap without a file-and-symbol citation is incomplete and will be rejected at the phase gate.

## Group 1 — Forward-progress surface

The single most useful operator signal during the incident was a hand-rolled `git rev-list --count base..HEAD` loop against agent worktrees. Watching that number climb, stall, or reset diagnosed three separate incidents within minutes each.

**1.1 Per-role forward progress in `get_status`.** For worktree-bearing roles, expose `{commits_ahead_of_base, last_commit_ts, last_commit_subject}`. The orchestrator already holds the worktrees locally; one git call per role. Where: the payload built in `orchestrator/routes/pipelines/_routes_status.py`. Acceptance: a running pipeline shows a non-null commits-ahead count per worktree-bearing role; roles without a worktree are absent rather than zero; a git failure degrades to null and never raises into the status route.

**1.2 Progress-regression detection in the overseer.** `commits_ahead` decreasing, or resetting to zero, without a corresponding branch push is never normal; it indicates either a discard or an agent re-deriving lost work. Raise a visible anomaly, not a log line. Where: `orchestrator/overseer/monitor/_anomaly_checks.py`. Acceptance: a simulated regression emits an `OVERSEER_ALERT` with a stable dedup key; a legitimate push that moves the base does NOT fire it.

**1.3 NACKed-but-not-re-proposing watchdog.** A producer heartbeat `WORKING` for ~37 minutes after two NACKs without ever re-proposing, then the consensus window expired. Time-since-last-NACK-without-producer-response is cheap and high-signal. Where: `orchestrator/overseer/monitor/_consensus_stall.py` (siblings `_check_post_consensus_stall`, `_check_incomplete_consensus_stall`; neither covers this). Acceptance: an unresolved NACK older than a configurable threshold with no intervening `CONSENSUS_PROPOSE` from the named producer emits an alert naming both roles.

## Group 2 — Event and alert feed

Destructive and exceptional events currently reach orchestrator logs or an alert counter only. An operator polling `get_status` sees none of them.

**2.1 `recent_events` in the status payload.** Last N warnings/anomalies for the pipeline. A `discarding unpushed local commits` WARNING, convergence-stall anomalies, and exhausted-key transitions were all log-only. Acceptance: bounded, newest-first, survives a status call during an active phase; bound configurable.

**2.2 `OVERSEER_ALERT` as a feed, not a counter.** The count climbed 10 to 52 across one run with no way to see contents or severity without pod/bus forensics, making genuine escalations indistinguishable from known false-positive noise. Acceptance: alerts surface with subject, severity, and dedup key; the existing counter remains for back-compat.

**2.3 Surface the stored `pipeline.error` string.** After a boot-race a pipeline was failed with a precise stored reason (`Failed to create worktrees ... gateway connection refused`) while `get_status` showed only `status: failed`. Acceptance: when the pipeline record carries an error, `get_status` returns it; null otherwise.

**2.4 Agent-side worktree health.** An agent detected `STILL UNMOUNTED` on its 1st through 23rd spawns and escalated; all of it stayed inside bus messages surfacing as a counter. Acceptance: per-role last heartbeat body (or a pod-side mount probe result) retrievable without reading pod logs.

## Group 3 — Clocks and per-invocation accounting

**3.1 Consensus-window countdown.** Nothing surfaces when the current slice's consensus window started or expires; two near-misses were computed by hand from log timestamps. The live-widening knob (#3494) is only useful if the clock is visible. Acceptance: `{consensus_window_started_at, timeout_minutes, expires_at}` per active slice, correct after a live timeout change.

**3.2 Per-invocation outcome summaries.** One-shot cycles that exit rc=0 having done nothing are indistinguishable from productive ones. Record `{role, duration, commits_made, consensus_action_taken, cost_usd}` per invocation; the SDK result event already carries most of it. For non-committing roles, "cycles without a consensus action" is the analogous metric. Note: `_usage_components` in `shared/egg_agent/client.py` captures `input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `output_tokens` but NOT `reasoning_tokens` (at `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`), while `config/litellm/cost_callback.py` does capture it. Close that asymmetry as part of this item. Acceptance: a no-op cycle is distinguishable from a productive one within 2-3 cycles; `reasoning_tokens` present in `AgentResult.token_usage`.

## Group 4 — Post-mortem durability

**4.1 Per-arm termination causes, queryable at any time.** `exit_code=75` crash-streaks had no queryable cause until a streak-10 escalation embedded them in a decision. The data exists in memory the whole time (`_format_exit_history` / `exit_history_text`, `orchestrator/event_loop/_supervisor.py:548`, `orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py:1387`) but is only rendered into log lines and streak-point escalations. Acceptance: recent terminations per dedupe key retrievable at any streak depth, including zero.

**4.2 Session-state TTL expiry as an event.** A 6h Redis TTL lapsing overnight converted a routine discard into an unrecoverable amnesia incident. `SESSION_STATE_TTL_SECONDS = 6 * 60 * 60` at `orchestrator/session_state_store.py:54`, refreshed on write, silent on expiry. Acceptance: "role X session state expired while its slice is active" is an event, not a silent reap. Consider whether active-pipeline session state should expire at all.

**4.3 Invocation transcript and log retention past pod exit.** Every diagnosis raced kubelet GC for pod logs and several were lost. Agents push transcripts to the session store ONLY on event-pod exit, so an agent that never exits has no stored transcript at all. This directly destroyed the decisive evidence in the incident motivating this work. Acceptance: `get_container_logs` and transcript retrieval work for completed one-shots, not only live pods; a long-running agent that has not exited still has a retrievable transcript.

## Constraints

- No behavioural regressions. Every new field is additive; existing consumers must not break.
- Tests per item, covering the success path and the degraded path (missing data, git failure, absent usage block).
- Never let a new surface crash an existing route. Status collection is advisory; on failure degrade to null and log, matching the existing `slice_admit` pattern in `_routes_status.py`.
- Concurrency: emit events outside scheduler locks; the injected-emitter pattern at `orchestrator/slice_scheduler.py:378` is the reference.
- Bounded: feeds and lists carry explicit caps; nothing unbounded enters the status payload.
- Distinguish null from zero. A missing measurement must not read as a real zero.

## Out of scope

Durable context-measurement tuning (#3249); token/cost accounting parity for the Anthropic route (#3508) beyond the `reasoning_tokens` asymmetry in 3.2; `cq-N` contract-decision surfacing (#3369); the overseer's own rate-limit crash-respawn loop (#3212).

## Background — context only, do NOT derive scope from these

The scope is the twelve items above and nothing else. These links contain historical narrative, superseded plans, and falsified hypotheses. Do not plan work from them. #3594 (backlog this spec supersedes), #3595 (incident analysis; its former root cause 1 was falsified and removed), #3364 (parent programme — its four-PR plan is complete and shipped, nothing in it is in scope).
